title: kernel-and-ldso-entropy-journal
content:
Notes-to-self: weird OOM pattern that shows after warmup + correlated ld.so activity / kernel messages. Trying to capture the breadcrumb trail (commands I ran, raw snippets, hypotheses, short repro).

Summary of symptoms:
- On gauss-prod-01 (A100-80GB), process serving model Y accumulates resident GPU memory over multiple requests and eventually hits an OOM (cudaErrorMemoryAllocation) even though aggregate token rate is low.
- Repro: not deterministic; often happens after a sequence of mixed short/long sequences (prefix caching suspected).
- Kernel dmesg sometimes shows NVML timeouts or Tainted modules with symbol versions mismatch around same time as OOM.

Why I think this is not a pure model leak:
- Restart process -> first 2-3 runs use expected memory, then growth starts after a particular request pattern.
- Running same model on a separate node with identical docker image usually fine -> points to node-level library/driver environment.

Hardware / SW baseline (prod node):
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 kernel 5.19.x (custom kube node image)
- Driver: NVIDIA 545.64 (installed via package manager)
- CUDA libs inside container: libcuda.so.1 symlinked to /usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64/stub/libcuda.so (suspicious)
- Container runtime: containerd 1.7 + nvidia-container-toolkit 1.12
- Runtime inside container: python 3.11, torch 2.2 + cu116 wheel (possible mismatch), custom serving-runtime build (PR 412)

Commands I ran (raw):
1) quick nvml / driver checks
$ nvidia-smi -q | head -n 80
Timestamp                           : Thu Mar 12 13:02:09 2026
Driver Version                      : 545.64
CUDA Version                        : 12.2
Attached GPUs                       : 1

2) check dynamic linking for process (pid 18542)
$ ls -la /proc/18542/map_files | head -n 5
(ran as root)

$ lsof -p 18542 | grep libcudart || true
python3 18542 user  mem    REG  259,1   15728640  /usr/local/cuda-11.6/lib64/libcudart.so
python3 18542 user  mem    REG  259,1    4030464  /usr/local/cuda-11.6/lib64/libcuda.so.1

3) ldconfig / ld.so anomalies
$ LD_DEBUG=libs /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import torch' 2>&1 | egrep "libcuda|cudart|openblas|ld.so" | head -n 30
... finding libcuda.so.1 => /usr/local/cuda-11.6/lib64/libcuda.so.1
... binding to /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 (0x00007f...)

Observation: python in container is binding to cuda 11.6 libs even though host driver is 545/12.2. This mismatch could cause symbol version differences (I saw similar in infra history notes).

4) kernel messages around failure (excerpt):
[2026-03-11T22:18:03] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, Ch 00000040, Class 0b0f, Fa 00000000, Pid 18542, GPU ce error
[2026-03-11T22:18:05] nvidia-modeset: Unloading driver module due to timeout

Also saw repeated: "module NVRM: loading failed, version magic mismatch" (got me thinking about mixed module builds).

5) reproducer attempts (container-level):
- baseline: start minimal container with /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6 and host /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu in LD_LIBRARY_PATH -> no OOM after 10k tokens.
- variant A: container binds to /usr/local/cuda-11.6 inside image (shippped wheel) -> OOM after ~2k tokens.
- variant B: set LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/cuda-11.6/lib64/libcudart.so -> immediate segfault in some worker threads.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Mixed cuda runtime / driver symbol versions -> some kernel calls timing out leading to NVML resets and memory accounting/shadow pages being inconsistent, causing eventual OOM. (High probability)
2) KV cache or allocator in serving-runtime leaking pinned host memory that bakes into GPU allocations via cudaHostAlloc and eventually fragments VRAM (medium).
3) Container shipped a copy of libcuda/libcudart that is incompatible with host kernel driver leading to surprising behavior under certain request patterns (highly plausible given LD_DEBUG).
4) MIG / compute-slice fragmentation combined with small allocations causing allocator behavior that triggers OOM (lower).

Interesting traces / snippets:
- python exception captured in logs: "cudaRuntimeGetVersion returned 3010 (cudaErrorUnknown) during cuCtxCreate"
- worker stdout: "E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:XXX] failed to allocate device memory: out of memory" (we don't use TF here but stack shows third-party lib linking)

Quick experiments to run next (ordered):
- Reproduce in stripped container: mount host /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu and do NOT ship cuda libs in image. If stable for 100k tokens, strong signal to disable shipped CUDA libs.
  Commands: docker run --rm -it --gpus all -v /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/host-libs:ro -e LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/host-libs:... image /bin/bash
- Force explicit CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and run small alloc stress: python alloc_stress.py (script below). Watch dmesg/nvidia-smi concurrently.
- On node: modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic, compare to module build-id to detect mismatch.
  $ modinfo nvidia | egrep "vermagic|intree|depends"
- Try running with NV_GPU_PERSISTENCE_MODE=0 vs 1 and see change.
- Use preloaded nvml trace: LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1 strace -f -e trace=network,openat -p 18542 (collect syscall patterns before OOM).

alloc_stress.py (very small reproducer):
import torch, time
model = torch.nn.Linear(1024,1024).cuda()
bufs = []
for i in range(1000):
    bufs.append(torch.empty((16,1024,1024), dtype=torch.float16, device='cuda'))
    if i%50==0:
        torch.cuda.synchronize(); print('iter', i, 'mem', torch.cuda.memory_allocated())
    time.sleep(0.1)

Notes on output of ldd on torch extension (.so file):
$ ldd _cuda_ext.so
\tlinux-vdso.so.1 (0x00007ffd4d5cc000)
\tlibcudart.so.11.0 => /usr/local/cuda-11.6/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0
\tlibcuda.so.1 => /usr/local/cuda-11.6/lib64/libcuda.so.1

This is the smoking gun for many runs: Python libs are pulling cuda-11.6 despite host being 12.x.

Edge cases / oddities observed:
- When swap is enabled on node (zram), the OOM sometimes turns into a kernel GPU reset and the container loses device node -> a few seconds later the node shows "NVRM: GPU reset succeeded". Not helpful for crash analysis.
- Some builds of our C++ extension show symbol version mismatch at load time (ldconfig warnings), probably because build container had libstdc++ from a different distro.

Quick mitigation sequence (if we see in production):
1) drain node (k8s) from scheduling for dedicated model tenants.
2) restart device plugin + kubelet (clean stale mounts)
3) run a controlled test container mounting host libs and run smoke workload to verify fix before returning to service.

Longer-term fixes to consider:
- Enforce that runtime images do NOT ship libcuda/libcudart; rely on host-provided driver libs and validate at startup (fail fast check comparing cudaDriverGetVersion and matched libcuda version).
- Add a preflight to serving-runtime startup: check ldd of native extensions and warn if path points to /usr/local/cuda-* inside image. Provide an environment variable to refuse to start unless they match host driver major version.
- Instrument allocator to emit per-tenant allocation deltas + periodic cudaMemGetInfo() snapshots to detect creeping allocations from third-party libs.

Random log snippet (raw) captured 2026-03-11T22:17:59:
[worker-12] WARN runtime.alloc: failed cudaMalloc(size=2147483648): out of memory (cudaErrorMemoryAllocation)
[host] ERROR nvml: nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex failed: 1 (NVMLError_Unknown)
[kernel] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus: GPU c2 (0000:65:00.0)

TODO / next-checklist:
- [ ] Reproduce on current node with host-libs mount (this afternoon), collect strace + ldd snapshots.
- [ ] Run quick binary diff between /lib/modules/*/kernel/drivers/video/nvidia* and packaged module in our infra images.
- [ ] Add startup check to serving-runtime that logs ldd of all .so in wheels (quick PR).
- [ ] Talk to infra about standardizing on driver 545.64 + container policy (no shipped cuda libs).
- [ ] Save a copy of crashing container image (image id) for offline bisect.

If I forget: the simplest repro is to run the same wheel that contains cuda-11.6 artifacts on a host with 12.x driver; if it crashes or slowly leaks, blame shipped libs first before digging into allocator internals.

End of this pass. Will append strace + dmesg captures here after the next run.

Maya
